title: CERT-In issues high-severity advisory on five WhatsApp vulnerabilities
date_note: The420.in says CERT-In issued the advisory on 26 November; Deccan Chronicle (27 November) gives no advisory date.
summary: India's CERT-In issued a high-severity advisory on five WhatsApp vulnerabilities, The420.in reports. Deccan Chronicle says the flaws include attachment spoofing, SQL injection and improper certificate chain validation, and that a specially crafted message, attachment or URL could let an attacker execute arbitrary code. The420.in says WhatsApp reported no evidence of exploitation for most of them, but acknowledged one weakness might have been exploited through certain spam messages.
plain: India's cyber agency warns of five serious WhatsApp flaws. A crafted message, attachment or link could let an attacker run code on a phone. Updating the app is advised.
exec: CERT-In rates five WhatsApp flaws high severity; a crafted message, attachment or URL could be enough to exploit them, per Deccan Chronicle.
action: As reported, CERT-In advises users to update WhatsApp to the latest version through their app store; the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre also advises logging out of WhatsApp Web manually.

sources.name: The420.in: WhatsApp Security Warning: CERT-In Issues High-Severity Warning Over Five Security Vulnerabilities
Deccan Chronicle: WhatsApp, ASUS Users Alert: CERT-In Flags Security Vulnerabilities

validation.note: The420.in and Deccan Chronicle, two independent publishers, each report the CERT-In high-severity WhatsApp advisory. The CERT-In page itself was not read; India Today's page would not load.
